A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same UniAug work. The main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original UniAug experiments on graph property prediction, link prediction and node classification, including scaling studies and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original UniAug experimental results and adds graph-classification comparisons in Appendix D.1, Table 13.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–B retain the same self-conditioned discrete diffusion model, graph-transformer/MLP denoiser, NOS guidance and task-specific augmentation procedures. No algorithm or objective change is documented.

E1.justification: The Network Repository/GitHub Star pre-training collection and downstream datasets and tasks are retained. All seven datasets in the new Table 13 already appear in v1 Table 2; the additional evaluation regimes do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 13 adds GraphCL and InfoGraph as evaluated comparators, alongside CtxtPred, InfoMax, JOAO and GraphMAE under additional settings. Comparator membership in the original main-text comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds graph-classification protocols involving within-dataset pre-training followed by split-specific fine-tuning, or self-supervised pre-training followed by SVM classification of graph embeddings. These supplement the existing cross-domain comparisons; the original experiments’ splits, metrics and model settings are retained.

E4.justification: The data/compute scaling studies, self-conditioning and guidance ablations in Table 7, homophily-group analysis, and guidance-objective comparison in v1 Table 14/v2 Table 15 are unchanged. New Table 13 supplies benchmark comparisons rather than an additional ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Existing mean/standard-deviation reporting and fold, run and split counts are retained. New Table 13 uses the established 10-fold cross-validation reporting convention; no new uncertainty-estimation practice, significance test or increase in repeated-run counts is reported.

E6.justification: All previously reported numerical result rows are retained. Table 13 adds alternative-protocol baseline results, including self-supervised GraphMAE’s 80.32 ± 0.46 on Collab alongside the reused UniAug result of 77.00 ± 2.02. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting performance changes from v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and Appendix A retain the same diffusion formulations, objectives and derivations. The transition matrices in Equation 7 are reformatted vertically without changing their mathematics; no new formal assumptions or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement in the introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: a cross-domain, data-scaling graph structure augmentor with plug-and-play benefits across node-, link- and graph-level tasks. The added comparisons support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a shared-topology explanation for cross-domain transfer and discusses limitations of feature-alignment approaches and baseline penalties from degree-only inputs. Section 4.2 shifts emphasis from data volume toward distribution coverage. Existing model-size and sampling limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly specifies random sampling of the existing 1,000 GitHub Star graphs, without establishing that the collection changed. Appendix D.1 documents the additional baseline procedures. Existing UniAug hyperparameters, hardware/optimizer information and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: Four references are added: L2-GCN, InfoGraph, the text-space graph foundation-model benchmark and the GCOPE paper. Appendix D.1 adds positioning against LLM-based feature alignment and dimension reduction. All original references are retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand the introduction and baseline discussion, refine the scaling terminology and add an equal-contribution footnote. The section hierarchy and Appendices A–E remain intact, without extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Visual revisions span all four figures: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2 is resized and restyled with revised ticks, title and caption, and Figures 3–4 receive new palettes. v2 also adds grouped Table 13, reflows existing displays and vertically stacks Appendix A’s transition matrices. This substantially updates the visual presentation while preserving existing plotted results.

improvement.justification: v2’s additional graph-classification comparisons and more explicit discussion of degree-only baseline inputs improve the context for assessing its comparative claims. The transfer and data-coverage explanations also improve clarity. The gain is limited: Table 13 changes training/evaluation regimes and does not isolate feature-removal effects or resolve baseline comparability for the other tasks.
